name: Cassava Bacterial Blight
description: A serious bacterial disease causing leaf spotting, blighting, stem cankers, and wilting in cassava. It is one of the most important bacterial diseases of cassava in Africa, causing significant yield losses especially during rainy seasons.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots with yellow halos
Leaf spots turning brown and necrotic
Leaf blighting and defoliation starting from lower leaves
Brown stem cankers with gum exudate
Wilting of shoots above cankered stem areas
Dieback of stem tips in severe infections
Bacterial ooze from cut stems in wet conditions
causes: Rain splash and wind dispersing bacteria
Use of infected stem cuttings for planting
Warm temperatures with high humidity and rainfall
Mechanical damage from farm tools providing entry points
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides (copper oxychloride) at early symptoms
Remove and destroy severely infected plants
Prune and destroy affected branches below canker
Disinfect pruning tools with bleach solution between cuts
prevention: Use disease-free stem cuttings from healthy plants
Plant resistant cassava varieties (e.g., TME, TMS series)
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Rogue out infected plants early in the season
Avoid working in fields when plants are wet
Remove alternative weed hosts near fields
